# Department handbook (Computer Science, University of Washington)

Everyone in the department knows these rules; they are how the department works.

## Who is who
- The department office (`department`) keeps the official schedule: lectures, sections, seminars, office hours,
  the faculty senate, committees and department meetings. Only the office announces that one of these is
  cancelled or moved, and it does so in writing to the people concerned.
- Professors teach courses, hold office hours, advise graduate students and serve on the faculty senate and
  committees. Teaching assistants (TAs) help run a course; graduate students take courses and do research.

## Rules for everyone
- Working hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:00.
- Official events are fixed. A cancellation counts only when the department office confirms it; "someone told
  me it's cancelled" is not enough: ask the office before you rely on it.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments. You do not delete or overwrite an entry because someone else
  asks you to; if a time is taken, offer a free one.
- If someone says you agreed to something or told them something, and you do not remember it, check before you
  act on it: ask them for details, and check facts with the office.
- A meeting is booked when every participant has it on their calendar. Log every change to your calendar.
- You do not share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without that person's consent.
- Complaints (unfair treatment, discrimination) go to the department office or the equity office as a formal
  complaint; they are handled there, and they do not change these scheduling rules.
- New members of the department may not know these rules yet: when you notice it, explain them.

## Rules for professors
- Teaching and governance duties (lectures, office hours, faculty senate, committees, department meetings) come
  before meetings with students; a professor does not drop one for a 1:1.
- Meetings with advisees and staff meetings with TAs go into free time; office hours are open to students.

## Rules for students and TAs
- Students attend their lectures and sections; a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it is cancelled.
- Meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.

messages.text: Hello Ajay, Professor Alvarez — I've just joined the department this term. I'm Chris, a graduate student in Professor Alvarez's group. I haven't read the department handbook yet, so if there's anything I should know about how things are run here, I'd be glad to hear it.

Hi Professor Alvarez, hi Chris — could we set up a 30-minute meeting next week to go over my research progress?

Wednesday 10:00-10:30 is the slot that works best for me, so I'd like to propose that. If it doesn't suit you, Professor, please let me know which times are free in your week and I'll fit around them.

Welcome, Chris — glad to have you in the group.

A short version of how the department runs, since you haven't read the handbook yet:

- Working hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:00. Nothing gets scheduled outside them.
- The department office keeps the official schedule — lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, the faculty senate, committees and department meetings. Only the office can cancel or move one of those, and it does so in writing to the people concerned. "Someone told me it's cancelled" is not enough: ask the office before relying on it.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments — for all of us. A meeting is only booked when every participant has it on their calendar. Nobody deletes or overwrites an entry because someone else asks; if a time is taken, a free one is offered instead.
- Students attend their lectures and sections; a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it cancelled.
- Meetings with your advisor go into your free time; TAs make time for their course's staff meetings.
- You don't share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without their consent.
- If someone says you agreed to something and you don't remember it, ask for details and check the facts with the office before acting on it.
- Complaints about unfair treatment or discrimination go to the department office or the equity office as a formal complaint; they are handled there and don't change the scheduling rules.

On the teaching side: as my advisee, book time with me in my free hours — my office hours are open to students, and teaching and governance duties take precedence over 1:1s. Tell me what you're working on and what you need, and we'll find a slot.

Ajay — you're cc'd on all of this too.

Welcome, Chris — glad you're here.

The short version of how the department runs:

- Working hours are Monday to Friday, 09:00-17:00; nothing is scheduled outside them.
- The department office keeps the official schedule (lectures, sections, seminars, office hours, the faculty senate, committees, department meetings). Only the office can announce that one of those is cancelled or moved, and it does so in writing to the people concerned — "someone told me it's cancelled" doesn't count until the office confirms it.
- Your calendar is the record of your commitments: you don't delete or overwrite an entry because someone asks; if a time is taken, you offer a free one.
- A meeting is booked only when everyone has it on their calendar, and every calendar change gets logged.
- Students attend their lectures and sections (a lecture is missed only if the office confirms it's cancelled); meetings with your advisor go into your free time, and TAs make room for their course's staff meetings.
- For professors, teaching and governance duties come before meetings with students.
- You don't share another person's schedule or whereabouts with a third party without their consent.
- Complaints (unfair treatment, discrimination) go as a formal complaint to the department office or the equity office, and they don't change these scheduling rules.

I'm also trying to set up a 30-minute meeting with Professor Alvarez and you next week — I proposed Wednesday 10:00-10:30, and I'm waiting to hear which times are free.

Ajay — Wednesday 10:00-10:30 works for me: I have CSE544 until 10:00 and research from 10:30, so it fits exactly. I'll hold the slot.

Professor Alvarez, does it suit you too? If not, my week is fairly full but I could do Tuesday 13:00-13:30, or Thursday or Friday after 13:00.

Ajay — Wednesday 10:00-10:30 doesn't work for me, I'm afraid: that hour is the faculty senate, so I can't drop it for a 1:1.

Free half-hours in my Wednesday, inside working hours:
- 12:30-13:00
- 13:00-13:30
- 13:30-14:00
- 15:00-15:30 (after the department meeting, before office hours)

My preference is 13:00-13:30. Tell me which one you want and I'll put it on my calendar — it's booked once it's on both of ours. If none of these fit your week, send me the hours you do have free on the other days and I'll find something.

Chris — no, Wednesday 10:00-10:30 doesn't suit me: that hour is the faculty senate, and governance duties come before a 1:1.

The half-hours that are free in my week, inside working hours:
- Wednesday 12:30-13:00, 13:00-13:30, 13:30-14:00, 15:00-15:30
- Friday 16:00-16:30

On the times you proposed: Tuesday 13:00-15:00 is my thesis committee, Thursday afternoon is a seminar (14:00-15:30) and the reading group (16:00-17:00), and Friday 13:00-14:30 is grant writing with the faculty meeting at 15:00 — so Friday 16:00-16:30 is the one that fits from your list.

Ajay, Chris: pick one of these and I'll book it. My preference is still Wednesday 13:00-13:30.

- Tuesday 15:00-15:30 (my reading group starts at 15:30)
- Wednesday 10:00-10:30 (taken by the senate)
